prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
The AI race is entering a difficult phase.

Governments and international bodies are building safety rules and review systems. At the same time, companies continue to train and release more capable models. The central question is not simply whether AI should move forward. It is whether safety work can move as fast as the technology.

Europe shows the tension clearly. Under the EU AI Act, obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models are already in application. Selected rules began enforcement, including rules on prohibited AI practices, some transparency duties, and general-purpose models. But the timetable is staged, not one switch for every obligation.

Elsewhere, the response is less uniform. The United Nations has created a scientific panel, but it does not make or enforce international law. In the United States, policy documents and proposals range from rapid, secure AI deployment to stronger testing and safety requirements.

These are different attempts to manage the same pressure: supporting AI innovation while making its development safer. That creates two clocks. One measures how quickly rules become real. The other measures how quickly models are trained, tested, and released.

【Point One】
EU obligations for general-purpose AI providers applied from 2 August 2025, and selected AI Act rules began enforcement on 2 August 2026. The UN panel gives nonbinding scientific assessments; its preliminary report said current safeguards cannot keep pace. U.S. measures here are executive policy, company proposals, or proposed legislation, not enacted federal law. A provider may therefore face concrete EU duties while the framework elsewhere develops.

【Point Two】
One company said it held back larger Astra runs while setting higher safety and security requirements, then restarted the large run on 28 August 2026. Google released a newer Flash model three weeks after the previous one, with updated safeguards. One safety institute reported that the best models’ success on cyber tasks rose from just over 10% in early 2024 to 50%, while task length doubled about every eight months. Another company says industry-wide pacing would need lawful coordination.

point_one.reasoning: EUの具体的な適用日・執行日、UNの非拘束性、米国措置が未成立の提案等であることを示し、地域によって提供者が直面する義務の確実性が異なると分かる。Full Storyの制度説明を、実際の法的拘束力と時期の差という具体的な含意まで深めている。

point_two.reasoning: Astraの大規模実行の延期・再開、Googleの短期間での新モデル投入、サイバー能力の上昇率など、AI開発の加速と安全対策の調整難を具体的な事例と数値で示している。単なる「技術と規制の二つの時計」の言い換えではなく、なぜ業界全体の協調やペース調整が必要になるのかを実証的に補強している。
